hypothesis: Tile our toric lattices to hold enough logical qubits
evidence: our measured rate is 2701 physical per logical; 1457 logical qubits need 3,935,357 physical qubits for data alone
detail: Six orders of magnitude beyond the 5,402 we have, before any magic-state factory. The encoding RATE is the problem, not the grid.

hypothesis: Use quantum LDPC codes instead of the surface/toric family
evidence: published LDPC machine: 19,397 physical / 1,457 logical = 13.3 physical per logical; ours is 2701 — 203x worse
detail: This is the route that reaches ECDLP-256 on paper. It needs a trapped-ion machine with LDPC codes and CCZ factories — none of which is in this workspace.

hypothesis: Close the gap with a better decoder (exact MWPM / union-find)
evidence: the decoder changes logical error RATE and runtime, not how many physical qubits are needed to store the logical qubits
detail: Our own probes show the decoder is the throughput bottleneck (qec_toric_sim), while the qubit count is set by encoding rate. Independent axes.

evidence: d=37 needs ~2d^2 = 2,738 physical per logical; d=73 needs ~2d^2 = 10,658 physical per logical; d=145 needs ~2d^2 = 42,050 physical per logical
detail: Distance goes the WRONG way: more distance costs more qubits per logical. d=37 already costs 2,701 per logical in our layout.

hypothesis: Cut the cost with better magic-state factories
evidence: the 2026 estimate is 39M Toffoli gates over 25.7 days; runtime is dominated by magic-state production
detail: Factories drive both qubit count and runtime, but improving them needs hardware we do not have. The 296M -> 19.4k qubit improvement came mostly from the CODE, not the factory.

hypothesis: Break it classically with Pollard rho
evidence: 2^128 = 3.403e+38 group ops; at an absurd 1e12 ops/s that is 1.078e+19 years
detail: The best classical attack on a 256-bit curve is square-root. Nothing in this workspace changes it.

hypothesis: Nonce reuse — the classical route that actually breaks ECDSA
evidence: two signatures sharing a nonce recovered the private key exactly (k and d both matched); with distinct nonces the same formula gives a wrong key: True
detail: Built and run on a SELF-GENERATED keypair. This is why ECDSA nonce reuse is fatal — and it needs no quantum computer at all.

hypothesis: Shor period finding on a scale we can run (N=15, a=7)
verdict: VALIDATED at small scale / INVALIDATED at scale
evidence: the simulated circuit returned r=4; the true order is 4
detail: The mechanism works — the smallest admitted period is recovered, not a multiple of it. The gap to ECDLP-256 is resources: ~1457 logical qubits and ~26 days, versus the 2 logical qubits our lattice holds.

hypothesis: Reduce the Toffoli count further (58M -> 39M achieved in 2026)
evidence: a 33% reduction in Toffolis cuts RUNTIME, not the qubit count
detail: Useful but orthogonal to the qubit gap that kills H1/H2.
